original_target.title: Beat factor two for scheduling on unrelated machines

full_original_statement: Input consists of $`m`$ machines, $`n`$ jobs, and nonnegative rational processing times $`p_{ij}`$ for running job $`j`$ on machine $`i`$. An assignment $`f:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,\ldots,m\}`$ has makespan $`C(f)=\max_i\sum_{j:f(j)=i}p_{ij}`$. Is there an absolute $`\varepsilon>0`$ and an algorithm, polynomial in the binary input length, that always returns $`f`$ with $`C(f)\le(2-\varepsilon)\min_g C(g)`$? A randomized algorithm succeeding with probability at least $`2/3`$ also counts.
